title: Major Depression with Suicidal Ideation
scenario: A 34-year-old male is brought to the emergency department by his sister after she found a note describing plans to end his life. He has a history of major depressive disorder and has been off his medication for several weeks.

lines: 34-year-old male brought in by sister. Sister reports finding a written note describing a plan to overdose on stored medication. Client is tearful, avoids eye contact, and speaks in a flat, slow voice. States 'everyone would be better off without me.' Reports not sleeping or eating for the past week and stopped taking his antidepressant about three weeks ago. Alert and oriented x3.

Client admits to active suicidal thoughts with a specific plan and access to a stockpile of acetaminophen at home. Denies current intent to harm others. Personal belongings searched and secured; no sharps or medications on person. Placed on continuous 1:1 observation.
Provider notified. Behavioral health consult and safety orders received. Client remains on 1:1 with environment cleared of hazards.

Client seen by psychiatry; voluntary inpatient admission accepted. States 'I'm glad someone is finally listening.' Contracted verbally to notify staff of any urge to harm self. Ate a small meal and rested for one hour. Remains on 1:1 observation.
Sertraline 100 mg PO daily (self-discontinued 3 weeks ago)
Remove all potentially harmful objects from the environment
Document suicide risk assessment each shift
Do not leave client unattended, including in the bathroom

children.subject: Mental Health
children.stem: Which 4 findings are cues that require immediate follow-up?

options.text: Statement that 'everyone would be better off without me'
A written note describing a plan to overdose
Reports not eating or sleeping for a week

children.rationale: A verbalized wish to die, a written suicide plan, neurovegetative symptoms, and stopping antidepressants all signal acute suicide risk. Normal orientation and oxygenation are not warning cues.

children.subject: Mental Health
children.stem: For each finding, click to specify whether it increases suicide risk, indicates depression severity, or both. Each finding may apply to more than one column.

rows.text: Specific plan with access to stockpiled acetaminophen
Hopeless statements about being a burden
One week of anorexia and insomnia

children.rationale: A specific, accessible plan is the strongest suicide-risk factor. Flat affect and neurovegetative symptoms mark depression severity, while hopelessness both deepens depression and raises suicide risk.

children.subject: Mental Health
children.stem: Complete the sentence. The nurse determines that the priority problem is {1}, so the priority action is {2}.
children.rationale: With an active plan and means, physical safety is the priority; continuous 1:1 observation prevents self-harm and outranks the nutrition and sleep problems, which are real but not immediately life-threatening.

children.subject: Mental Health
children.stem: For each intervention, click to specify whether it is indicated or contraindicated for this client.

rows.text: Remove sharps, cords, and belts from the room
Maintain continuous 1:1 observation, including in the bathroom
Ask directly about suicidal thoughts and plans
Place the client in a private room at the end of the hall away from staff
Assure the client his statements will be kept strictly confidential from the team

children.rationale: Removing hazards, constant observation, and direct questioning are core suicide-precaution measures. Isolating the client away from staff and promising secrecy both endanger safety and are contraindicated.

children.subject: Mental Health
children.stem: As the nurse implements the plan of care, which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.

options.text: Keep the client within view at all times
Use a calm, nonjudgmental tone and allow the client to express feelings
Document a suicide risk assessment and secure the environment
Tell the client to focus on positive thoughts and cheer up
Leave the client alone in his room to rest without observation

children.rationale: Constant observation, therapeutic communication, and documented risk assessment protect the client. Minimizing his feelings and leaving him unobserved remove the safety net and are inappropriate.

children.subject: Mental Health
children.stem: Which findings indicate the plan of care has been effective? Select all that apply.

options.text: Client verbally contracts to notify staff of urges to harm himself
Client ate a small meal and rested
Client remains safely on 1:1 observation with no self-harm
Client continues to state he has a plan to overdose at home

children.rationale: Engaging with treatment, agreeing to a safety plan, resuming basic self-care, and remaining free of self-harm show progress. A persisting active suicide plan would signal continued risk, not improvement.
